doc.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997

title: Armed Forces Network broadcasts from Wiesbaden
summary: Copyists and Tony Bennett as librarian; weekly hour-long live broadcast from the Wiesbaden Opera House; Masso wrote constantly and saw little of Germany then.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you have to do the copying and all that yourself?

As a matter of fact, and Tony Bennett will admit to this. He was a librarian. He used to come down and pick up the scores from me, take them to the copyist — we had a copyist and that’s all he did for the band. Our job was to perform once a week over the Armed Forces Network for the troops. We put on an hour broadcast. And all week long we rehearsed for that.
Did you do live performances also?
I meant, actually what I meant was with an audience, a dance?
Yes there was an audience all the time. It was held in the Wiesbaden Opera House, in Wiesbaden, Germany. And there was an audience every Sunday.
How is it with the German population? How did they, I mean I assume you’d get out around the town a little bit.

Not in those days, Monk. No. In fact I spent practically all of my time just writing. I was so engrossed in it, and it was such a great opportunity. I just loved it. So we didn’t really get out, at that time, and get a feel of what was going on with the German people. Later on, I’ve done several tours in Germany in the last fifteen years, and that has given me a good feel of what it’s like on the other side, and how they feel about jazz, and actually performing with some of them.
